title: Enable hardware RT request for realistic flashlight live mode
objective: Update the flashlight live teleop workflow so --live-lighting-mode realistic actively requests hardware ray tracing / Lumen hardware ray tracing where the package/RHI supports it, applies ray-traced shadow intent to the spawned spotlight when possible, and logs enough runtime/readback state for the user to verify whether RT actually took during their next simulator run.
instructions: Read the Scout result .control-tower/packets/inbox/scout-63b476db-9744-4726-8f03-968ca6f8cbdb-result.json before editing.

Inspect examples/flashlight/run.py, examples/flashlight/flashlight_profiles.py, examples/flashlight/flashlight_profiles.json, and tests/test_orbit_collection_validation.py for existing profile/runtime-render patterns.

In realistic live mode, request hardware ray tracing explicitly in both launch INI/config and runtime console-command application. At minimum this should include r.RayTracing.Enable=1 alongside the existing Lumen GI/reflection settings; add the relevant Lumen hardware tracing CVars only after verifying names from local engine/project context or stable Unreal docs/comments.
Add a CLI escape hatch such as --disable-hardware-ray-tracing or equivalent so the user can fall back if their package/RHI rejects RT. Keep realistic mode defaulting to hardware RT requested.

Attempt to set ray-traced shadow intent on the spawned ASpotLight component when hardware RT is requested, using robust reflected-property/method probing in the existing helper style. Do not assume one API name; report applied/failed state in logs.

Add startup/runtime logging that clearly distinguishes requested RT settings from confirmed/applied readback. The logs should help the user identify cases like Vulkan SM5 / RT unavailable even if commands were requested.
Keep default non-realistic mode behavior unchanged.
Update or add focused unit tests for CLI defaults/overrides, config string composition, and profile/runtime state where feasible without launching Unreal.
Do not run Unreal, cook, package, or any long process. User will run the simulator manually.
Return the exact command the user should run after the change, including the hardware RT default and how to disable it if needed.
constraints: Do not edit docs unless a tiny README/running-example note is necessary to keep the user command accurate; prefer reporting the command in the ResultPacket.
expected_outputs: ResultPacket summarizing code/tests changed, validation commands run, and the exact user test command.
definition_of_done: Realistic live mode requests hardware RT by default with a disable flag, spotlight RT shadow intent is attempted/logged, tests pass, and user has a command to run.
